assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Himadri Speciality Chemical (consolidated, Rs crore). Three business lines: (1) core carbon materials and chemicals (coal tar pitch, carbon black incl. speciality, naphthalene, oils, SNF, new speciality chemicals) plus the captive power plant's external sales; (2) Others: Birla Tyres and mining; (3) new energy materials (LFP cathode, anode). EBITDA follows the company definition (before forex and other income); history from Screener is after forex (FY26 forex loss Rs 43.6 cr), so the Excel reconciliation row shows the forex. We assume no forex gains or losses. Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS.

segments.name: Carbon materials & chemicals (incl. captive power)
segments._why: Volume x realisation. Standalone volume 564 kt in FY26 (+2%); Q1FY27 132 kt (-6% YoY) but realisation ~Rs 96,600/t (+23%) as higher raw-material costs after the West Asia crisis were passed on. Capacity was ~80% used in Q1 with 90%+ expected in FY27 (new 70 kt speciality black line at 85-90%, distillation debottlenecked to 600 kt, liquid-pitch exports, anthraquinone/carbazole from Q2FY27). We assume volume +6% / +8% / +5% (600 / 648 / 680 kt) and realisation +11% / -2% / +2% (prices ease from Q1's peak): revenue +17% / +6% / +7%. Q1FY27 core revenue was +15% YoY.
segments._marginWhy: Core EBITDA per tonne (consolidated core EBITDA / standalone volume): Rs 4,400 FY22, Rs 13,400 FY24, Rs 15,300 FY25, Rs 17,300 FY26, ~Rs 23,700 in Q1FY27 (helped by price rises and the new speciality line). We assume Rs 20,500 / 21,000 / 21,500 per tonne (FY27E-29E), i.e. Q2-Q4FY27 back to ~Rs 19,600 as raw-material prices settle, then mix gains from SSCB, CNT and anthraquinone. That is a 24.0% / 25.0% / 25.1% margin on our revenue (FY26 22.3%, Q1FY27 24.2%).

segments.name: Others: Birla Tyres and mining
segments._why: Others segment revenue Rs 274 cr in FY26 (Birla Tyres Rs 187 cr from the May-2025 restart; the rest mining). Q1FY27 Rs 144 cr (tyres ~Rs 127 cr), with mining stopped pending an environmental clearance (3-6 months). Management targets Rs 3,000 cr of tyre revenue in 4-5 years. We assume tyres ~Rs 590 cr in FY27 (quarterly sales rising from Rs 127 cr to ~Rs 170 cr) plus a little mining in H2: Rs 620 cr; then +66% and +45% (Rs 1,030 cr and Rs 1,490 cr), about half of management's path by FY29.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA Rs 27.9 cr in FY26 (10%), mostly mining profit (Q4FY26 EBIT Rs 25.4 cr); Q1FY27 EBIT Rs 1.2 cr with no mining. Management expects tyre EBITDA break-even in FY27. We assume 2% / 5% / 7%: a sub-scale tyre maker with a revived brand, well below the 12-15% of established tyre companies.

segments.name: New energy materials (LFP cathode, anode)
segments._why: No battery-material revenue in FY26 (the base of Rs 1 cr is notional: the engine needs a non-zero base). Anode: 200 tpa plant from Apr-2026, revenue potential Rs 120-130 cr, samples at stage B of four (approval takes 1.5-2 years). LFP: 2,000 tpa in Q3FY27, Phase 1 of 40,000 tpa built over the following ~12 months, FY29 the first full year; ~Rs 3,000 cr revenue at full use (~Rs 7.5 lakh/t). We assume Rs 20 cr in FY27, Rs 350 cr in FY28 (~4,000 t of LFP plus anode samples) and Rs 1,000 cr in FY29 (~12,000 t, 30% of Phase 1): customer approvals and Chinese price parity are the constraints.
segments._marginWhy: Start-up losses in FY27 (about -Rs 25 cr on two small plants), break-even-ish in FY28 (-3%) and 8% in FY29. Management prices at par with China and says it has a cost edge but discloses no margins; an analyst on the Q1 call calculated a negative spread at Chinese prices. Chinese LFP makers have earned thin margins in the price war.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: EBITDA per tonne holds near Q1FY27's level as speciality black, SSCB, CNT and anthraquinone lift the mix; Birla Tyres follows management's path; LFP approvals arrive on time.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Raw-material prices fall and EBITDA per tonne slips back towards FY26's ~Rs 17,000; tyres stay sub-scale; LFP approvals slip a year and the plants run at a loss.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: P/E on Sep-28E EPS (half FY28E, half FY29E). The only institutional broker, ICICI Securities, uses a sum of the parts with the core on FY28E EV/EBITDA; for a company with net cash and little interest that carries the same information as P/E, its other parts are not public, management guides on profit (Rs 1,100 cr+ PAT in FY28) and retail brokers use P/E. 25x = HSCL's one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 (24.9x, no trough years excluded). No sector cut: listed chemicals trade ~28% below their five-year medians, but HSCL's median already includes 2021-23 at 8-13x, when peers were at their richest. Growth (our EPS +15% a year FY26-29E) and returns (ROE ~16-17% vs a 12.5% cost of equity, negative free cash flow in FY27-28E) do not justify a premium.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Close to ICICI Securities' method for the core business: 15x FY28E EV/EBITDA in Apr-2026 (12x in Jan-2026). HSCL's own trailing EV/EBITDA median since 2021 is ~23x, ~17x one year forward at our EBITDA growth. 16x Sep-28E EBITDA plus net cash and investments at Sep-27E (model basis).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 12-year FCFF at 12.5% (cost of equity = WACC with net cash), terminal growth 5.5%; working capital held at the FY26 ratio of revenue (~29%).

cover.headline: A coal-tar champion priced as a battery-materials company: the profits have not caught up with the price
cover.lead: Himadri turns coal tar, a by-product of steel-making, into pitch for aluminium smelters and graphite electrodes, carbon black for tyres and plastics, naphthalene and speciality oils. It is India's largest pitch maker (65%+ share) and has quadrupled its EBITDA per tonne since FY22, taking net profit from ₹39 cr to ₹755 cr. Now it is spending ~₹2,000 cr on battery materials (LFP cathode, anode), carbon nanotubes and a revived tyre brand (Birla Tyres). The only institutional broker, ICICI Securities, values it on a sum of the parts with the core on EV/EBITDA; we use **P/E: 25x Sep-28E EPS of ₹20.9** (its own forward median since 2021), which gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**, so **we initiate with SELL.** EV/EBITDA (₹489) agrees; the DCF (₹330) is lower still. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The core business has been transformed
arguments.p: EBITDA per tonne rose from ~₹4,400 (FY22) to ₹17,331 (FY26) and ~₹23,654 in Q1FY27, on speciality carbon black (now 130 kt), better pitch grades and cost control. ROE is ~18% and the company is net cash. This is a well-run, integrated business.

arguments.h: But growth was margin, not volume, and margins can turn
arguments.p: Revenue was flat from FY23 to FY26 and volume grew 2% in FY26; Q1FY27 volume fell 6% while prices rose 23% on costlier raw materials. We assume EBITDA per tonne eases to ~₹20,500 in FY27. The new capacity (pitch exports, anthraquinone, SSCB, CNT) is real but small next to a ₹4,400 cr core.

arguments.h: The new bets are early and capital-hungry
arguments.p: LFP (₹1,125 cr) starts with a 2,000 t plant in Q3FY27 and has no disclosed orders; the company prices at par with China. Tyres absorbed ~₹490 cr of NCD funding for ₹187 cr of FY26 revenue at break-even. Free cash flow turns negative in FY27-28E on our numbers, and ROE dips to ~16%.

arguments.h: The price already pays for success
arguments.p: At ₹678 the stock trades at 35.2x our FY28E EPS and 42.9x trailing (five-year median 39.1x), while listed chemical peers trade a median 28% below their medians. Valuing the core at 16x EBITDA, the market implies ~₹10,400 cr for battery materials that have yet to sell.

sections.title: One coal-tar chain, three businesses

blocks.p: Coal tar is a sticky by-product of the coke ovens that feed steel blast furnaces. Himadri buys it from steel makers and importers and distils it (600,000 tpa; the largest single-location complex in the world, per the company). About half becomes **coal tar pitch**, the binder in the carbon anodes of aluminium smelters and in graphite electrodes. The lighter fractions become **naphthalene** (for phthalic anhydride, SNF concrete admixtures and mothballs) and **speciality oils**, which also feed its own **carbon black** plants (tyres and rubber, plus speciality grades for plastics, inks, cables and batteries). A captive power plant runs on carbon-black tail gas. Exports were 29% of FY26 revenue (61 countries). On top of this core sit two new businesses: **Birla Tyres** (restarted in May-2025) and **new energy materials** (LFP cathode and anode for lithium-ion batteries).

sections.title: Coal tar is a by-product business; carbon black and batteries are global commodities

blocks.p: Coal tar supply is set by steel-making, not by demand for pitch: every tonne of metallurgical coke yields a few per cent of tar, so supply grows with India's blast-furnace steel output and imports fill the gap. Demand comes from three places. **Aluminium smelters** need pitch to bind their carbon anodes (India is adding smelter and refinery capacity). **Graphite electrodes** for electric-arc steel use pitch as binder and impregnant (an oversupplied industry: HEG and Graphite India earned 3-7% ROE in FY26). **Carbon black** for tyres is a ~15 mn t global market growing ~2-3% a year, of which speciality grades (~1.1 mn t) grow ~4% (Notch Consulting via the annual report). Battery materials are a different world: China makes essentially all LFP cathode and most anode material, and cell-component prices fell 50-60% in 4-5 years.

bullets: **What drives it.** Volume (capacity ~80% used in Q1FY27, 90%+ expected in FY27) times realisation (raw-material costs are passed on with a lag) times the mix of higher-value products. The company does not disclose product-wise volumes or prices, so we cannot split pitch from carbon black or oils.

**Q1FY27.** Standalone volume 131,844 t (-6% YoY) but revenue +16%: coal tar and oil prices rose after the April-May West Asia crisis and Himadri passed them on. **New capacity.** Distillation debottlenecked from 500 kt to 600 kt; liquid pitch terminals at Haldia and Mangalore; anthraquinone and carbazole (2,600 tpa in Q2FY27, 5,300 tpa by Q2FY28, ₹248 cr capex); CNT 200 tpa (Q4FY27, ₹70 cr). Management says there is no further capex in distillation.

sections.title: Carbon black: the move to speciality grades is the real story of FY22-26

blocks.p: Carbon black is fine soot made by burning heavy oil in a controlled way; ~90% of the world's output goes into tyres and rubber. Speciality grades (for plastics, masterbatch, inks, coatings, cables and battery electrodes) need tighter control of particle size and purity and sell at higher prices per kilogram, not per tonne. Himadri makes its own feedstock oil from coal tar, which is its edge. It has 250 kt of carbon black capacity, of which 130 kt is speciality after a 70 kt line (₹220 cr) started in FY26, sold under nine brands (Energex and Electra for batteries, Jetex for cables, Klarex and Colorx for plastics and inks, among others). Next: 6,000 tpa of **super speciality black** (₹170 cr, Q4FY28), converted from commodity rubber-black lines, which management says carries margins "significantly higher" than speciality.

blocks.p: Birla Tyres was a well-known bias-tyre brand that went bankrupt. In Oct-2023 Himadri and Dalmia Bharat Refractories (DBRL) won it in insolvency; the plant restarted on 29-May-2025. On 21-Sep-2026 the boards approved a scheme to demerge DBRL's tyre business into HSCL (1 HSCL share per 260 DBRL shares; FY26 turnover of that business ₹149 cr), which would simplify this. The focus is agri, off-the-road (OTR) and truck-bus bias tyres, with a radial car-tyre (PCR) plant for EVs and SUVs planned by FY28.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Himadri has a **narrow moat in coal tar processing and pitch**: scale, integration and customer approvals that a new entrant cannot copy quickly, in a market where supply is tied to steel. In carbon black it has a cost edge from its own feedstock but competes with global majors on quality. It has **no moat yet in battery materials or tyres**, where most of the new capital is going. Margins in the core still move with raw-material spreads, as FY21-22 showed.

sections.title: Flat revenue, five-fold profit: FY22-26 was a margin story

blocks.p: Himadri's numbers fall into two eras. Until FY22 it was a coal tar processor with thin, volatile margins: in FY21-22 raw-material costs ran ahead of prices, the EBITDA margin fell to 6% and net profit to ₹39 cr. Since then revenue has gone up only 67% (₹2,791 cr to ₹4,661 cr, and almost flat from FY23 to FY26), but EBITDA rose six-fold and net profit nearly twenty-fold to ₹755 cr. The driver was EBITDA per tonne: about ₹4,400 in FY22, ₹17,300 in FY26 and ~₹23,700 in Q1FY27, as more of the coal tar went into speciality carbon black, high-grade pitch and oils, and costs came down. Q1FY27 revenue rose 28% (₹1,432 cr) and net profit 27% (₹228 cr), the first quarter with real top-line growth.

blocks.p: For four years Himadri spent little on plants: capex was ₹23-171 cr a year in FY22-25, so most of the ₹1,619 cr of operating cash in FY22-26 went to paying down debt and building cash. That changed in FY26 (capex ₹450 cr, the 70 kt speciality black line) and changes more in FY27-28: management plans ~₹1,000 cr of capex in each year (LFP ₹1,125 cr, tyres ~₹500 cr, CNT, SSCB, anthraquinone). The other big use of cash has been investments outside the plant: ₹1,029 cr of investments bought in FY24-26, mainly Dalmia Bharat Refractories NCDs that fund the Birla Tyres plant (₹487 cr at Mar-26), IBC, Sicona and mutual funds. bullets: **Forex inside expenses.** The company's EBITDA (₹1,006 cr in FY26) excludes forex; the P&L books forex in other expenses (FY26 loss ₹43.6 cr, Q1FY27 loss ₹25.2 cr). Screener's EBITDA (₹962 cr) is after the loss.

**Other income.** ₹171 cr in FY26 (₹52 cr FY25; ₹56 cr in Q1FY27): interest on deposits partly funded by short-term borrowing (borrowings rose from ₹313 cr to ₹770 cr in FY26), mutual-fund gains and fair-value gains on IBC, Sicona and Birla Tyres instruments. It was 17% of FY26 pre-tax profit.

**Fair-value gains in other income.** Of FY26 other income of ₹171.3 cr, ₹100.0 cr was a fair-value gain on non-current investments carried at fair value through P&L (IBC, Sicona and similar; ₹0.2 cr in FY25); interest on bank deposits was ₹43.5 cr. Excluding the fair-value gain, FY26 pre-tax profit would have been ~10% lower.

**Net cash definition.** Company net cash ₹121 cr at Mar-26 (Q4 call; the Jul-2026 deck shows ₹113 cr), down from ~₹371-392 cr at Mar-25 despite record profit, as capex, strategic investments and working capital absorbed cash.
**Cash conversion.** Screener: cash from operations ₹382 cr in FY26 vs EBITDA ₹962 cr (40%); inventory days rose from 68 to 96.

**Consolidation by control.** Invati (40%) and Himadri Birla Tyre Manufacturer (49%) are consolidated as subsidiaries on contractual control (Ind AS 110), so tyre revenue is consolidated while the tyre plant sits in DBRL until the demerger.

**Related parties.** Himadri carries ₹183 cr of optionally convertible preference shares in Modern Hi-Rise, its own promoter holding company (a 1% non-cumulative instrument from a 2018 amalgamation; the issuer decides on conversion or redemption). Small stakes in group companies Himadri Credit & Finance and Himadri e-Carbon.
**Tyre funding off the operating line.** The Birla Tyres plant is funded through ₹487 cr of DBRL NCDs shown as investments, not capex; the demerger will bring the assets onto Himadri's balance sheet.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** The audit (Singhi & Co) is unqualified and segment data reconcile. The amber is for the size of other income (17% of FY26 pre-tax profit, over half of it fair-value gains), cash from operations at only 40% of EBITDA in FY26, a sizeable investment in the promoter's holding company, and tyre funding routed through investments.

Three business lines: (1) core carbon materials and chemicals (coal tar pitch, carbon black incl. speciality, naphthalene, oils, SNF, new speciality chemicals) plus the captive power plant's external sales; (2) Others: Birla Tyres and mining; (3) new energy materials (LFP cathode, anode). segments.name: Carbon materials & chemicals (incl. captive power)
segments._why: Volume x realisation. Standalone volume 564 kt in FY26 (+2%); Q1FY27 132 kt (-6% YoY) but realisation ~Rs 96,600/t (+23%) as higher raw-material costs after the West Asia crisis were passed on. Capacity was ~80% used in Q1 with 90%+ expected in FY27 (new 70 kt speciality black line at 85-90%, distillation debottlenecked to 600 kt, liquid-pitch exports, anthraquinone/carbazole from Q2FY27). We assume volume +6% / +8% / +5% (600 / 648 / 680 kt) and realisation +11% / -2% / +2% (prices ease from Q1's peak): revenue +17% / +6% / +7%. Q1FY27 core revenue was +15% YoY.
segments._marginWhy: Core EBITDA per tonne (consolidated core EBITDA / standalone volume): Rs 4,400 FY22, Rs 13,400 FY24, Rs 15,300 FY25, Rs 17,300 FY26, ~Rs 23,700 in Q1FY27 (helped by price rises and the new speciality line). We assume Rs 20,500 / 21,000 / 21,500 per tonne (FY27E-29E), i.e. Q2-Q4FY27 back to ~Rs 19,600 as raw-material prices settle, then mix gains from SSCB, CNT and anthraquinone. That is a 24.0% / 25.0% / 25.1% margin on our revenue (FY26 22.3%, Q1FY27 24.2%).

segments.name: Others: Birla Tyres and mining
segments._why: Others segment revenue Rs 274 cr in FY26 (Birla Tyres Rs 187 cr from the May-2025 restart; the rest mining). Q1FY27 Rs 144 cr (tyres ~Rs 127 cr), with mining stopped pending an environmental clearance (3-6 months). Management targets Rs 3,000 cr of tyre revenue in 4-5 years. We assume tyres ~Rs 590 cr in FY27 (quarterly sales rising from Rs 127 cr to ~Rs 170 cr) plus a little mining in H2: Rs 620 cr; then +66% and +45% (Rs 1,030 cr and Rs 1,490 cr), about half of management's path by FY29.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA Rs 27.9 cr in FY26 (10%), mostly mining profit (Q4FY26 EBIT Rs 25.4 cr); Q1FY27 EBIT Rs 1.2 cr with no mining. Management expects tyre EBITDA break-even in FY27. We assume 2% / 5% / 7%: a sub-scale tyre maker with a revived brand, well below the 12-15% of established tyre companies.

segments.name: New energy materials (LFP cathode, anode)
segments._why: No battery-material revenue in FY26 (the base of Rs 1 cr is notional: the engine needs a non-zero base). Anode: 200 tpa plant from Apr-2026, revenue potential Rs 120-130 cr, samples at stage B of four (approval takes 1.5-2 years). LFP: 2,000 tpa in Q3FY27, Phase 1 of 40,000 tpa built over the following ~12 months, FY29 the first full year; ~Rs 3,000 cr revenue at full use (~Rs 7.5 lakh/t). We assume Rs 20 cr in FY27, Rs 350 cr in FY28 (~4,000 t of LFP plus anode samples) and Rs 1,000 cr in FY29 (~12,000 t, 30% of Phase 1): customer approvals and Chinese price parity are the constraints.
segments._marginWhy: Start-up losses in FY27 (about -Rs 25 cr on two small plants), break-even-ish in FY28 (-3%) and 8% in FY29. Management prices at par with China and says it has a cost edge but discloses no margins; an analyst on the Q1 call calculated a negative spread at Chinese prices. Chinese LFP makers have earned thin margins in the price war.
